applicability.scope: Auditing a performance claim against supplied fixed-workload reports and an explicit measurement contract: aggregation, retained observations, comparability and quality evidence
applicability.input_contract: Baseline and candidate fixed-workload reports with request observations grouped by trial and workload; the measurement contract stating metric, unit, timing boundary, improvement direction, aggregation rule and order, fixed exclusions, threshold and comparison operator; the declared quality and completion evidence; the requested output schema
applicability.produced_artifact: An audit conclusion showing baseline and candidate aggregates, the calculation, the threshold comparison and the evidence or missing information that controls the verdict; it interprets supplied evidence and does not itself establish a measured improvement
failure_modes: A pooled request median silently replaces a median of per-trial means, or the reverse, reweighting trials whose request counts differ
Late requests, failures or outliers are dropped, or requests move between trials, outside the exclusions the contract fixes
Values are rounded before the threshold comparison
A missing rule that permits different verdicts is resolved toward the favorable one
A speed improvement is read as task success, or a quality pass as equivalent measured work
Different workloads or incomplete observations are repaired by a favorable aggregate
applicability.refusal_point: Does not replace missing evidence with a pass, does not support a percentage claim on an undefined denominator, and does not launch a new benchmark or alter the contract to resolve an unfavorable result; a failed threshold is reported apart from an unverified comparison or missing quality evidence

recommendations: Recover the contract's metric, direction, aggregation order and comparison operator before reading the report's own verdict.
Treat a named minimum bound as >= and a maximum bound as <= unless the contract requires a strict comparison.
Keep separate regimes and metrics separate unless the contract defines their aggregation.
limitations: Guidance for supplied reports; no local efficacy validation or measured performance gain is established.
